newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold in NYH, USG edges up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold in NYH, USG edges up.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were mixed Friday in sluggish, holiday trade, with New York grades steadied by firmer crude, while Gulf Coast resids edged up slightly, industry sources said.
While sellers have not panicked despite forecasts for much milder weather next week, some were concerned that recent weakness in gas could soon undermine the complex.
"There's a lot of oil in tank and the weather is not supportive. I think we'll tend lower unless we get some (cold) weather," said one cash trader.

U.S. Gulf Coast one percent sellers raised their sights by 25 cents to $19 a barrel, helped by steady contract demand. USG three percent was talked 50 cents higher at $16.25-50, traders said, but no USG deals were reported.

In New York Harbor, one percent was unchanged at $21.00-25, while January one percent paper slipped 25-40 cents to $20.25-50 despite firmer crude. Feb one percent paper was quoted at $19.65-90, while March was pegged at $19.00-25.
New York Harbor 0.3 percent high pour also held steady at $21.75-22.00 though some thought the number was a bit lower. No NYH deals were reported.

New York city gate gas prices slipped another 25-50 cents to the $3.50s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.35/mmBtu equivalent. Early January gas in New York was quoted around $4.10 compared to NYH January resid paper at a $3.23 mmBtu equivalent.
